title: Payment Operations Note: Lapsed-Grace Deduction on a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Returned-Payment Late Charge
content:
**Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract — when the return was recorded late in or after the grace period.**

**Rule.** The return lag is the number of calendar days from the re-opened installment's due date (the installment the contract's next due date shows) to the date the most recent returned payment was recorded (returns recorded on the same date share that date). When the return lag is greater than the product's grace period of 10 days, so that the grace period had already ended before the customer learned of the return, 2.00 dollars are deducted from the re-opened installment late charge; when the return lag is greater than 5 days but not greater than the 10-day grace period, 1.00 dollar is deducted; in every other case nothing is deducted.

The grace period read here is the product's late-charge grace period: 10 calendar days on Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Tier 5, Tier 4, Tier 3, Tier 2, Tier 1 and Tier 1+ alike. The deduction is taken from the re-opened installment late charge once the late-charge cap has been applied, and the charge after the deduction is never below zero.

**Counting.** A count of calendar days from one date to another is the second date less the first, so the first date is not counted and the second is; the count is zero or negative when the second date is not after the first.

## Ladder

| Return lag (calendar days from the due date to the return) | Deducted |
|---|---|
| 11 or more | 2.00 dollars |
| 6 to 10 | 1.00 dollar |
| 5 or fewer, zero, or negative | nothing |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Due date the 1st, return recorded on the 11th of the same month: lag 10, not greater than 10, so 1.00 dollar. Recorded on the 12th: lag 11, so 2.00 dollars.
- Due date the 1st, return recorded on the 6th: lag 5, not greater than 5, so nothing; recorded on the 7th: lag 6, so 1.00 dollar.
- A return recorded before the due date gives a negative lag: nothing is deducted.
